name: 30739-randomdecode-8b-4gpudp
hardware: 4x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 of ONE node (--gres=gpu:4), sm90, NVLink between the four cards. Driver 570.195.03.
parallelism: DP=4, TP=1, PP=1 -- four data-parallel replicas of the whole model, one per GPU, behind one front end. The width is part of the setup: fewer cards, or the same four at TP=4, is a different setup.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=200, bounded at 4000 requests with a 1200 s safety cap, warmup the first 10%, no cooldown, static seed 30739.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets. Prompt EXACTLY 128 tokens and output EXACTLY 512 (min = max, held there by `ignore_eos`), so a pass is a fixed 512k prompt tokens in and 2.05M tokens out. `request_format: plain`, so no chat template is applied.
purpose: An 8B chat assistant writing 512-token replies to short prompts for 200 concurrent users on four GPUs.
launch:
# The engine's command line. The engine is a source checkout of commit 08f425bad168, named
# directly by `configs/env.yaml: venv`.
model: Qwen/Qwen3-8B

# Four data-parallel replicas on four GPUs of one node, one per card, each a complete copy of the
# model (~16.4 GB). No tensor split. `data-parallel-size-local` and `data-parallel-rank-local` are
# both left unset, which puts all four replicas on this node behind one front end.
data-parallel-size: 4
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# PINNED, AND LOAD-BEARING -- these are NOT the values an unpinned run of this deployment takes.
# Do not drop either as "the default": without them the scheduler runs at 2048 batched tokens and
# 128 sequences, admitting 16 of these 128-token prompts per step instead of 64.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 1024

# The workload's worst case is 128 + 512 = 640 tokens, against the checkpoint's own 40960 window.
max-model-len: 2048

dtype: bfloat16
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
